Article.ArticleTitle: Knowledge regarding Hepatitis B Mother-to-child Transmission among Healthcare Workers in South China.

Abstract.AbstractText: To determine the knowledge regarding hepatitis B virus mother-to-child transmission (MTCT) and its prevention and treatment among healthcare workers in Guangdong province, China, an Hepatitis B virus endemic area. An HBV knowledge questionnaire was administered to 900 healthcare workers (HCWs) from the 3rd Affiliated Hospital of Sun Yat-Sen University and two rural hospitals in Guangdong province. The 27 items in the questionnaire fell into three sections: HBV mother-to-child transmission general knowledge, respondents' practices of preventing HBV mother-to-child transmission, awareness of the resources of preventing HBV mother-to-child transmission. The data collected was coded and analyzed using SPSS software version 20. In total, 503 of 900 healthcare workers responded to the survey (response rate: 55.9%). Eighty-four individuals responded correctly to all of the knowledge questions: 58 were doctors, and 26 were nurses (P<0.05). Doctors more often performed practices than nurses (t=3.591, P<0.01). Participants from the infectious disease department demonstrated a significantly higher proportion of correct answers and resource utilization than other specialties (χ2 =14.052, 7.998, P<0.01). In terms of the average knowledge score, t test or ANOVA showed that there were significant differences between the specialty groups (t=3.110, P<0.01), hospital level groups (t=2.337, P<0.05) and age groups (F=3.020, P<0.05). Respondents' initiative increased with hospital level and age (t=2.993, 7.493, P<0.01). A considerable percentage of HCWs has misconceptions about HBV mother-to-child transmission. Healthcare workers, in particular, nurses, those working in non-infectious disease departments or township hospitals and younger medical staff lack systematic and comprehensive knowledge about HBV mother-to-child transmission, and are in urgent need of HBV-related training.
